stories.headline: EPPO investigation into election IT systems prompts Siliņa to demand action plan; ministry official suspended
stories.summary: Following European Public Prosecutor's Office (EPPO) findings of alleged irregularities in election IT procurement, Prime Minister Siliņa gave the Smart Administration Minister three weeks to produce a digital governance reform plan, called the current system 'ossified,' and the Education Ministry's IT department director was suspended pending a service review. Opposition figures including Armands Puče accused the ruling coalition of attempting to manipulate upcoming elections.

stories.headline: NBS activates emergency alert after Ukrainian drones approach Latvian airspace during attack on Russian port
stories.summary: In the early hours of Sunday May 3, the National Armed Forces issued a cell-broadcast emergency alert for five eastern border regions (Alūksne, Balvi, Ludza, Rēzekne, Krāslava) warning of a possible airspace threat. The alert was lifted roughly three hours later; NBS subsequently stated the objects detected by its sensors were most likely Ukrainian drones en route to attack the Russian port of Primorsk.

articles.title: Possible airspace threat in Latvia's east is over

stories.headline: Government approves two Kurzeme wind farms but delays K2 Ventum amid public opposition and corruption allegations
stories.summary: After PM Siliņa announced on social media that the K2 Ventum wind farm project in Dienvidkurzeme would need additional public consultation, the Cabinet on April 28 approved environmental impact assessment for the Eko Ziemeļi and Kurzeme projects while deferring K2 Ventum. Climate Minister Melnis stated politicians should not be deciding on individual wind farm projects, and the PM rejected allegations that political influence had been purchased.

stories.headline: PM Siliņa's 2025 income declaration published, showing 5.3% salary increase to €133,615
stories.summary: Multiple outlets reported on the State Revenue Service's publication of PM Evika Siliņa's 2025 income declaration, showing she earned €133,615 as head of government — a 5.3% increase over 2024 — and owns one apartment and co-owns land in Riga.

stories.headline: Latvia transfers additional CVR(T) armoured reconnaissance vehicles to Ukraine
stories.summary: The Latvian Cabinet of Ministers approved the transfer of additional CVR(T) tracked armoured reconnaissance vehicles to Ukraine on April 28, with Defence Minister Andris Sprūds stating the transfer would continue 'for as long as necessary' to support Ukraine against Russian aggression.

stories.headline: Latvia marks 36th anniversary of independence restoration; President Rinkēvičs addresses Constitution anniversary
stories.summary: President Edgars Rinkēvičs issued a address on the anniversary of the convening of the Constitutional Assembly, stating 'Latvia's story is and will be ours to shape.' Separately, the National Armed Forces held its Freedom Celebrations Day (NBS diena) in Aizkraukle to mark the May 4 restoration of independence.

stories.headline: Siliņa visits eastern border; border guard chief warns of active summer on Latvia-Belarus crossing
stories.summary: PM Siliņa visited the eastern border region on May 1 to discuss the current migration situation, accompanied by a large entourage. State Border Guard head Guntis Pujāts said the approaching summer would not be peaceful, with rising numbers of illegal crossings as weather improves.

articles.title: Busy summer expected along Latvia's eastern border

stories.headline: Siliņa faces public criticism and Prosecutor-General inquiry over €4,000 VIP airport lounge use in Amsterdam
stories.summary: PM Siliņa received public criticism after TV3's programme '900 Seconds' revealed she and two aides used a VIP lounge at Amsterdam Airport Schiphol costing over €4,000. A public survey gave her communications on the matter an average rating of 2.4 out of 10, and the Prosecutor-General ordered an inquiry on the basis of a KNAB referral.

articles.title: Sabiedrība neapmierināta ar Siliņas skaidrojumiem par VIP zāļu izmantošanu
Ģenerālprokuratūra pārbaudīs Siliņas VIP zāles izmantošanu ārzemēs

stories.headline: Latvian media runs multiple articles on NATO cohesion, Article 5, and summit frequency amid US-Europe tensions
stories.summary: Multiple Latvian outlets published analytical pieces on NATO unity challenges — discussing whether a member state could be expelled, lessons from the Iran war for NATO readiness, and proposals to reduce the frequency of annual summits. Coverage reflects heightened attention to alliance stability in the context of US-European tensions.

stories.headline: Latvijas Banka and Bank of Lithuania launch EU-funded anti-fraud financial literacy plan
stories.summary: The Bank of Latvia, in cooperation with the Central Bank of Lithuania, OECD, and the European Commission, launched an action plan under an EU Technical Support Instrument project to protect residents from financial fraud. A workshop was held April 24 presenting data on the current fraud situation in Latvia.

articles.title: Finanšu krāpšana nerimst: Latvijas Banka veido plānu iedzīvotāju aizsardzībai
Latvian central bank to run financial literacy campaign

stories.headline: Rinkēvičs meets Health Minister, directs faster action on medication access for cancer and diabetes patients
stories.summary: President Rinkēvičs met with Health Minister Hosam Abu Meri and called on him to work with health sector organisations to address unmet medication needs for Type 1 diabetes and oncology patients. A public petition on ManaBalss.lv was also launched demanding statutory rights to state-funded effective medicines while over 7,000 patients remain on waiting lists.

stories.headline: Latvian and Estonian leaders' joint call for EU Russia-dialogue envoy draws criticism in Estonia
stories.summary: Ukrainian media reported that earlier in 2026, PM Siliņa and Estonian President Alar Karis jointly called for the appointment of an EU special envoy to conduct talks with Russia. The call drew criticism from Estonian Social Democrat leader Lauri Läänemets, who called Karis's remarks about dialogue 'irritating.'

articles.title: Estonian president criticised over remarks on dialogue with Russia

stories.headline: Wind turbine collapses in Bunkas, subsequently robbed of generator and copper
stories.summary: A wind turbine owned by SIA 'Jaunmiki' collapsed in Bunkas pagasts, Dienvidkurzeme. Officials including Climate Minister Melnis visited the site. It was subsequently reported that thieves used heavy machinery to steal the main generator and non-ferrous metals from the downed turbine.

stories.headline: ECB holds interest rates steady; Latvian coverage notes implications for mortgage holders
stories.summary: The European Central Bank held rates at current levels at its Frankfurt meeting, as reported in both the ECB's Latvian-language press conference statement and Latvian media analysis noting the implications for Latvia's borrowers, particularly those with home or car loans, given that eurozone inflation rose to 3% in April.
